findings.claim: 86 counts pull-request/decision hits over 20 decisions, and --base listed 11 of them as unverified; the prototype README and the ADR's Rejected item called them 86 decisions and said --base found 0.
the ADR said the base-branch checkout keeps a pull request from loosening the audit, though the same pull request can edit the workflow.

verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed.
The prototype README and the ADR now count 86 hits (pull request and decision pairs), say they cover 20 decisions, and say `--base` listed 11 only as `unverified`, none for a changed source.
The ADR now says the base-branch checkout makes loosening the audit a visible workflow change, not that it prevents it.
The gates are green.
Gates: I ran `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree.
Format, tests, integration and eval rows r1, r2, r3, r5, r7, r8, r9, r10, r11 and r12 pass, ending "stamp green: 893d4bcc14d26e801f1a180e06dff284d2fa870e6a81708d258608bfa1311c05".
f1: I read `git diff --cached main` for both files and checked the numbers against the totals in `results.txt` (86 hits, 11 listed, 75 missed, 0 with a source-changed reason, 59 file and 16 folder).

The prototype README's Results say "86 hits ... counted once per pull request and decision ... 20 distinct decisions", "listed 11 of the hits, none for a changed source: each was listed as `unverified`", and the Conclusion says "none of the 86 hits for a changed source".
The ADR's Context (lines 29-33) says "86 times a pull request changed a file that a stable decision names" and "listed none of the 86 for that reason".
The Rejected item (lines 133-136) says it "listed none of the 86 times a pull request changed a decision's source for that reason".
A grep finds no "found 0" or "86 decisions" left in the ADR, the prototype index or the log.
f2: ADR lines 61-72.

They say GitHub runs the pull request's own workflow file, that the checkout does not stop a same-repository author from changing it, that it "makes loosening the audit a visible change" which review and branch protection see, and that it does not guard the API key.
This agrees with the Consequences item on prompt injection.
I found nothing new in the touched text that breaks the rest of the record.
